dependencyAudit.note: High and critical root advisories require an exact GHSA ID, vulnerable range, installed lock version, reachability argument and an unexpired review window of at most 30 days. New advisories on an accepted package fail. Stale acceptances and reported fixed advisories fail. audit:ci alone contacts the registry; the normal gate is offline.

advisories.reachability: build time only, but genuinely executed: this is the bundler behind `npm run web` and `npm run build:web`, and it reads every image asset in the repo.
advisories.resolution: @expo/metro 56.0.0 pinned metro 0.84.4, which depends on image-size. 56.0.2 pins metro 0.84.5, which dropped image-size altogether. ~56.0.0 is the range expo already declares, so 56.0.2 needed no override — only a lockfile that was not stale. `npm update @expo/metro` moved exactly one version and added nothing else; the full suite and a real `npm run build:web` both pass on 0.84.5.

advisories.reachability: install time only. adm-zip is required by exactly one file, onnxruntime-node/script/install-utils.js, run from that package's postinstall to unpack the ORT native binary out of a .nupkg fetched over TLS from api.nuget.org. The tutor agent's runtime path is onnxruntime-node/dist/binding.js, which only require()s the prebuilt .node addon — grep for adm-zip under dist/ finds nothing. A crafted ZIP therefore needs control of NuGet or a broken TLS chain, not a learner.
advisories.resolution: 2026-10-04: exact scoped onnxruntime-node -> adm-zip 0.6.1 override replaces the vulnerable install-only ZIP parser. Public npm metadata and a clean onnxruntime-node1.24.3 fixture verify the tested release and integrity. The installed constructor, getEntry and extractEntryTo API remain compatible with the native installer; bounded forged-size and symlink extraction checks exercise security fixes. Existing dependency versions and platform binaries are preserved. A clean root manifest npm ci fixture verifies the committed lock; paid voice lifecycle remains a separate acceptance check.

advisories.reachability: not reached. The advisory is a missing bounds check in v3, v5 and v6 when a caller supplies its own buf. Rechecked 2026-11-02 against the installed xcode 3.0.1: its only use of uuid is `uuid.v4()` at lib/pbxProject.js:90 (generateUuid), with no buf argument, and no source file under apps, packages or services imports uuid at all. The chain is also build time only: xcode writes Xcode project files during an Expo prebuild, and ios/ and android/ are gitignored here.
advisories.why: The fix is uuid >= 11.1.1 against xcode 3.0.1 declared ^7.0.3. xcode 4.0.0 (now published) drops uuid entirely, but the SDK 57 @expo/config-plugins declares xcode ^3.0.1; only @expo/config-plugins for Expo SDK 58 moves to ^4.0.0, and npm audit offers the fix only through expo 58, a semver-major SDK upgrade. Not worth forcing for an unreachable call site. Moderate, so `npm run audit:ci` reports it rather than failing on it. Revisit with the SDK 58 upgrade.

advisories.reachability: on-device only. react-navigation decodes deep-link paths and query strings through query-string, so a crafted link opened by a learner can reach the quadratic percent-decoding. The worst case is that learner freezing their own app. No server, service runtime, minutes or other learner is reached: no app server or service imports query-string or decode-uri-component.
advisories.why: Fixed in 0.5.1, but query-string 7.1.3 declares ^0.2.2 and @react-navigation/core declares query-string ^7.1.3, so no lockfile-only update exists. A fix needs query-string 10 (which drops this package) through a react-navigation upgrade, or an override to 0.5.1, a version query-string never declared. Revisit at the next react-navigation upgrade.

advisories.chain: @luvani/brain -> zod; @luvani/tutor-agent -> zod, @livekit/agents, openai; @anthropic-ai/sdk -> zod; expo -> @expo/cli -> zod
advisories.reachability: not reached from caller input. Checked 2026-11-02: only packages/brain source imports zod; services/tutor-agent and services/token-server define no zod schemas, and token-server request bodies are not validated with zod. The one constrained collection is ScenarioFrameSchema.beats .min(1) (plus a numeric min/max in typesafe.ts), and those schemas parse LLM structured output from Anthropic or OpenAI, bounded by the request token limit, not learner or caller payloads. Dependencies use of zod (SDK tool schemas, LiveKit, Expo CLI) was not audited line by line.
advisories.why: Fixed only in 4.6.6, a major upgrade. Our ^3.24.1 ranges could move, but @anthropic-ai/sdk, openai, @livekit/agents and @expo/cli all declare zod 3 ranges, so a fix needs a coordinated zod 4 migration. Revisit with the zod 4 migration, and before any zod schema with collection limits validates caller input.
